system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: Figure 4 shows the prompt template for our type predictor.
system_prompt_style.note: Paper-only. Each module fills a prompt template with {code}, {path}, {types} and {prev_code}. The linked repo (walkccc/LeetCode) is the dataset source, not the harness.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: All keys and queries are encoded to vectors using the Sentence-BERT [21] model, and we use the L2-norm as the distance metric for retrieval.
env_context_strategy.note: Retrieval returns Z3 templates from a knowledge base, not snippets of the repository. The program under test is injected into the prompt in full.

context_compaction.note: Paper only; no code or config was available to show where compaction would be declared.

observation_format.evidence_quote: We input the buggy code and the error message into an LLM, and ask it to fix the code.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: we first concatenate it with the previously generated code and then execute it.
tool_call_format.note: The LLM writes Z3Py code, which the harness executes.

edit_primitive.note: No file-editing surface is described; paper only.

protocol_standardization.note: Built on AutoGen per Sec. 4.1; no protocol is mentioned.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: If the initially generated Z3 code is buggy, the code generator will try to fix it using a self-refine mechanism.
loop_primitives.note: Fixed stage order: type inference -> per-chunk Z3 generation with execute-and-fix -> test case generation, with fallback to the LLM solver.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: We implement the LLM-Sym agent using the AutoGen [33] library.
multi_agent_topology.note: Specialised LLM modules (type predictor, Z3 generator, test case generator, LLM solver) hand off in a fixed sequence.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: we introduce a variable environment to store the SSA indices for each variable.

long_term_memory.note: The static hand-built template knowledge base is few-shot retrieval, not memory.

self_verification.evidence_quote: we execute the generated code to check whether it contains bugs.
self_verification.note: Closest value: the harness executes the generated Z3 code, not tests.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: we keep tying this self-repair process 3 times for each chunk.
retry_policy.note: Attempts are capped at 3 per chunk; if all fail, the path goes to the LLM solver as a fallback.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: If the LLM solver predicts that a path cannot be satisfied, it will terminate generating the answer

cost_controls.note: Model assignment is fixed per module (GPT-4o-mini for most modules, GPT-4o for the test case generator); it is not routing.

eval_hooks.note: The linked repo is the LeetCode solutions dataset source, not the harness.

target_domain.evidence_quote: LLM-Sym is capable of solving path constraints on Leetcode problems
target_domain.note: The domain is symbolic execution and test case generation for Python programs.

open_source.note: The harness code is not in the evidence. The MIT licence belongs to the dataset repo walkccc/LeetCode.

model_agnostic.note: Only GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini are used.

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: The Python solutions are collected from a public GitHub repository https://github.com/walkccc/LeetCode.
primary_artifact.note: The mapped repo is the dataset source, not the harness code.

first_release_date.note: Based on the paper v1 date; no harness repo was available.

pinned_version.note: No harness repo; the provided pin 9b85aa15e086 is the LeetCode dataset repo.

stars.note: The 1337 stars belong to walkccc/LeetCode, not to the harness.
